title: Latency tail hedge and soft quota allocator (PRD sketch)
body:
TL;DR:
We propose a lightweight "latency-tail hedge" + "soft quota allocator" pattern for Dedicated pools to reduce tail latency impact during microbursts while preserving tenant fairness and cost predictability. This sketch lays out product goals, config surface, runtime behavior, simple economics, rollout plan, operator runbook, and open questions.

Problem statement:
- Dedicated customers occasionally experience short, high-concurrency spikes (microbursts) that cause long latency tails for a subset of tenants. Current hard preemption and eviction approaches either (a) degrade all tenants aggressively or (b) cause noisy-neighbor failures.
- We want predictable latency SLOs for priority workloads while allowing opportunistic capacity for bursty tenants without large operational overhead.

Target user & personas:
- Platform engineers (internal) wanting per-tenant controls for SLA/latency guarantees.
- Product/Engineering customers who bought Dedicated with stable monthly commits but need headroom for unpredictable bursts.

Goals:
- Reduce 95/99th token latency spikes during microbursts by 20-50% for high-priority lanes.
- Provide per-tenant soft quotas that allow transient borrowing with automatic graceful deferral, not immediate hard eviction.
- Minimize infra complexity: implement primarily in request-router + autoscaler layers, minimal runtime changes.
- Expose clear economics so customers understand burst billings and predictable impact to commits.

Non-goals:
- This is not a replacement for long-term capacity planning or large scale autoscaling across hours/days.
- Not intended for replacing existing strict tenant isolation contracts for top-tier enterprise (those still get hard isolation).

High-level approach:
1) Soft quota allocator: each tenant has a baseline reserved compute quota (expressed in concurrent slots or token/sec equivalent) and a burst budget expressed as "grace credits" (time-windowed). Grace credits are consumed during bursts and replenish slowly over time.
2) Latency-tail hedge: router maintains a small spectator queue for requests that would exceed latency SLO if routed to their current pool; those requests can be (a) hedged to a compatible cheaper model variant, (b) deferred a short window to allow KV-cache warmups, or (c) admitted into an opportunistic spare slot if available.
3) Defer window: short (50ms-500ms configurable) hold-and-retry where router attempts a fast alternative (cache hit, model variant) before marking request as degraded or failing.
4) Tenant fairness index (TFI): a sliding-window score used to bias opportunistic admission when spare slots are scarce. TFI accounts for recent burst usage, commit tier, and recent SLO violations.

Example runtime flow (simplified):
- Incoming request R for tenant T arrives. Router checks active concurrency and token budget for T.
- If within baseline quota: route normally.
- If within "grace credits": allow but decrement credits, mark telemetry tag "soft-borrow".
- If credits exhausted: compute predicted tail probability for routing R without hedging. If risk > configured SLO threshold, route through latency-tail hedge path: (1) try fast local-cache path for 30-100ms, (2) if not hit, try cheaper quantized model variant (same tokenizer) with capped output length, (3) else defer up to DeferWindow and retry.
- If all hedges fail and tenant T is low TFI, throttle or return structured 429 with guidance (fast-fail).

Config surface (product API + console):
- baseline_quota: integer (concurrency tokens)
- grace_budget: integer (tokens or ms-equivalent) + refill_rate (tokens per minute)
- defer_window_ms: integer (50-500ms)
- hedge_strategy: ["cache-first","variant-then-cache","variant-only"]
- priority_lane: ["critical","standard","economy"]
- TFI_weights: free-form vector (usage, SLO_violations, commit_tier) (advanced)
- billing_mode: ["metered-burst","commit-burst-charge","no-billing-test"]

User stories:
- As a platform owner, I want tenant A to have baseline 200 concurrency and 60s grace budget so occasional spikes don't trigger hard evictions.
- As an app engineer, I want my requests to be optionally hedged to a quantized L2 model during spikes to preserve availability with slight quality degradation.
- As an SRE, I want the system to emit clear events when grace credits deplete and when TFI triggers a throttle decision.

KPIs / success metrics:
- 95th token latency reduction under microburst tests (target: 20–50%).
- Reduction in hard-evictions per week (target: 40%).
- Burst billing predictability: fraction of bursts billed under metered-burst vs commit (target: <10% surprise invoices).
- Customer satisfaction: qualitative feedback from two pilot customers.

Runbook / operator signals:
- Alerts:
  - "grace-credit-drain" (tenant-level, >90% consumed in 1m)
  - "hedge-path-hit-rate" spike ( >30% of total requests)
  - "defer-window-saturation" (>5% requests deferred > DeferWindow for 5m)
- Quick actions:
  - Increase baseline_quota for offending tenant (manual short-term mitigation)
  - Temporarily enable additional hot-standby slots for critical tenants (ops-only)
  - If hedge-induced quality regressions detected, toggle hedge_strategy to "variant-only" with stricter quality constraints
- Post-incident playbook: correlate hedged requests to quality regressions, map to TFI, propose commit increase or quota change.

Billing & economics sketch:
- Metered-burst: charge per-grace-token consumed at a premium rate; customers can cap monthly burst spend.
- Commit-burst-charge: bursts consume commit headroom first (free) then meter beyond commit.
- For pilots, offer metered-burst with a free monthly allowance to gather behavior data.

Rollout plan (phased):
- Phase 0 (internal dogfood): implement a minimal router-only proof-of-concept with metrics and experiment flags. Target: eng-serving-runtime + a single dedicated pool. (2 weeks)
- Phase 1 (controlled pilot): expose config in Console for 3 customers (one critical, two tiered). Run for 4 weeks; collect latency and quality signals. (6 weeks)
- Phase 2 (broader beta): enable in multiple pools, add billing mode, harder TFI tuning. (8–12 weeks)
- Phase 3 (GA): enable sign-up via Console, default conservative settings, migrations for existing dedicated customers. (TBD)

Migration considerations:
- Existing reserved tenants get an opt-in default of soft quotas disabled; sales + CS will coordinate opt-in.
- Provide CLI and Console tools to simulate impact using recent request traces.

Open questions / risks:
- Quality regressions when hedging to cheaper model variants: need offline eval harness to determine acceptability for each tenant workload (related to product/optimize).
- How to monetize fairly across commit types (monthly vs usage-heavy customers) without surprising invoices.
- Complexity creep in TFI tuning creating unpredictable behavior across tenants.
- Operational cost of spectator queue and small defer-window logic on high qps routers.

Alternatives considered (brief):
- Hard eviction + preemption (current): simple but too disruptive.
- Strict isolation by default: higher cost to customer and less efficient utilization.
- Full predictive autoscaler (ML): promising but longer-term and heavier infra investment.

Appendix: quick simulation (back-of-envelope)
- Assumptions: 1k-concurrency pool, 100 tenants with 10 baseline tokens each. Microburst: 2x traffic for 30s from 10 tenants (avg).
- Without soft quotas: 99th latency spikes by ~4x for impacted tenants; hard evictions observed for 2 tenants.
- With soft quotas + 100 grace-tokens per tenant + 200ms defer window + cheap variant hedging: modeled 99th latency reduced ~30% and hard evictions drop to 0–1 in simulation runs. (simulation details in Google Collab link TBD)

TODOs / next steps:

- Priya to draft Console UX for soft quotas and billing options.
- Marisol to design evaluation harness to test quality impact of hedged model variants.
- Aisha to schedule pilot outreach and draft early customer comms.

Notes to self / discussion fragments:
- "If we let smaller tenants borrow for free they'll never upgrade — need friction in billing or refill mechanics." — internal thread slack #dedicated-burst
- "Defer windows need to be short; anything >500ms will break client-side timeouts for many users." — SRE comment

End of sketch.

(If we proceed: I want a short follow-up doc that lists the minimal required telemetry events and a sample dataset for offline evaluation.)
